title: Joy
lead: Joy in the Bible is gladness in God and in what he does, often in the middle of trouble: the joy of Israel's feasts and psalms, of the good news in the Gospels, and of Paul writing from prison to the Philippians.

sections.b: Philippians uses 'joy' and 'rejoice' about sixteen times in four chapters, though Paul is in chains and a friend has nearly died: 'Rejoice in the Lord at all times. Again I will say it: rejoice!' (Philippians 4:4). The reason for joy is the Lord and his work, not good circumstances.
sections.refs: Philippians 1:4; Philippians 1:18; Philippians 2:17-18; Philippians 3:1; Philippians 4:4; Philippians 4:10

sections.b: Joy belongs to Israel's feasts and worship, to the psalms, to the prophet who rejoices though the fig tree fails, to the angels' good news at Jesus' birth, and to the fruit of the Spirit.
sections.refs: Deuteronomy 16:14-15; Nehemiah 8:10; Psalm 16:11; Habakkuk 3:17-18; Luke 2:10; Galatians 5:22; 1 Thessalonians 5:16
